topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: Library vs. Key-Value Store
lecture_lines: Transformers use Attention for context and relationships.
MLPs serve as the model's long-term memory.
Think of the MLP as a vast fact vault.
animations: Display text 'Library Analogy' at center, color #FFFFFF.
Show bookshelf graphic, highlight shelf, color #FFFF00.
Show key-value table, highlight key, color #00FFFF.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Neuronal Key-Value Mechanism
lecture_lines: MLPs function like Key-Value storage systems.
An input Query activates specific memory neurons.
The neuron outputs a Value to the stream.
animations: Show neuron diagram, highlight synapse, color #FFFF00.
Fade out diagram, keep title, color #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Mechanics: Weights as Fact Templates
lecture_lines: Weights define the MLP's fact templates.
Layer one acts as a pattern matcher.
Layer two functions as the fact generator.
A vector input triggers a specific neuron spike.
The neuron projects the fact to the output.

sections.title: The Overlapping Fact Storage
lecture_lines: Facts are stored in weight superpositions.
Multiple facts share the same neuron clusters.
Memory is distributed like a hologram.
animations: Overlay two patterns on grid, color #FFFF00.
Fade out pattern one, keep grid, color #00FFFF.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: The network is an associative memory system.
Inputs map directly to factual completions.
MLP neurons act as the knowledge retrieval.
Patterns trigger the storage of specific facts.
This structure enables efficient fact retrieval.
animations: Final summary fade to black, color #FFFFFF.
